key_insight: The paper replaces biased mini-batch normalizers in large-scale Cox regression with a softplus-based surrogate that enables unbiased single-sample gradients and sharper convergence guarantees.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to scale survival-model training on large datasets while preserving statistical fidelity, including asymptotic agreement with the full Cox estimator.
method: Introduce one auxiliary scalar per LogSumExp normalizer and optimize a softplus surrogate with unbiased stochastic gradients.
Prove improved optimization rates for smooth convex objectives: O(T^-1/2) averaged objective error and ~O(T^-1) last-iterate squared error with a strongly convex regularizer.
For Cox regression, group neighboring failures and share one auxiliary variable per group to exploit nested risk-set structure and control approximation error.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic and real survival datasets with slowly decreasing risk sets show favorable performance compared with stochastic baselines.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on how well grouped risk sets and the softplus approximation capture the full Cox normalizers, so grouping granularity may need careful tuning.
paper_title: Scalable Cox Regression via Grouped Risk Sets and Sharper LogSumExp Rates
